idiom_name: dlopen/dlsym over the dynamic loader search path (name services: getaddrinfo)
implementation_notes: libc already contains the pattern's mediating instance instead of a structure to build: dlopen() loads a shared object by name through the loader's search order (DT_RPATH, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, /etc/ld.so.cache maintained by ldconfig, /lib and /usr/lib) and dlsym() resolves a symbol name to its address, so the dynamic linker performs name-to-location resolution and a dlclose/dlopen pair is the re-resolution step. For network resources getaddrinfo() is the name service: it combines host and service name resolution into one call and returns a list of socket addresses, using the platform resolver with its own caches (nscd, resolver TTLs). What stays manual is the binding table and its policy: a process-local name-to-handle cache, its TTLs and its invalidation must be written by hand, and a single dlsym/getaddrinfo call at startup often makes the whole structure unnecessary.
pitfalls: dlerror() must be cleared before the call and read immediately after each dlopen/dlsym/dlclose; a stale error is indistinguishable from a fresh one.

dlclose() unmaps code while function pointers resolved from it may still be reachable - calling them is the C form of a stale binding; keep the handle alive for as long as any resolved pointer can be used.
getaddrinfo() allocates the result list, so a missing freeaddrinfo() leaks on every resolution, and the temporary failure EAI_AGAIN must not be handled like the permanent EAI_NONAME.
